title: Enriched system adjunction from the actual counit and projection
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X	o Y$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $W=X,Y,\overline X$ and $	au=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathscr S_W^	au$ be the category of strict systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and componentwise morphisms [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]; use its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact evaluations $e_n$ and, for $m\ge n\ge1$, derived quotient functors $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Write $t^M_{m,n}:T^W_{m,n}M_m	o M_n$ for the scalar-extension adjunct of the actual transition. 
Work first on etale systems and let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $a_W:W	o s$. Suppose $F=Rp_{*, ullet}j_{!, ullet}\dashv G$ is an actual adjunction, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$, and suppose the canonical system maps $a_Y^*P\otimes^LFM	o F(a_X^*P\otimes^LM)$ are invertible for every coefficient-system test $P$. Let $M$ on $X$ and $N$ on $Y$ be normalized systems with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and assume $FM,GN$ have these same properties. Use derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the mapping-system notation of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Define $\widehat{\mathcal H}_W(U,V)=Ra_{W,*, ullet}^{\mathrm{et}}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathscr S_W^{\mathrm{et}}}(U,V)$, representing $P\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(a_W^*P\otimes^LU,V)$.
The tensor-Hom/projection/adjunction bijections for all $P$ define a natural isomorphism in $D(\mathscr S_s^{\mathrm{et}})$
$$\widehat\Phi_{M,N}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_Y(FM,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{\mathcal H}_X(M,GN).$$
With the transpose convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], its defining adjunction transpose uses the actual counit $FGN	o N$. Its inverse equations hold as coefficient-system morphism equations. If evaluation identifies $F\dashv G$ counit-compatibly with the finite adjunctions, each evaluation of $\widehat\Phi$ is the finite derived mapping-complex adjunction. On degree-zero Hom the forward and inverse maps are $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_NF(g)$. Under the canonical identifications of the underlying towers of $\widehat{\mathcal H}_Y(FM,N)$ and $\widehat{\mathcal H}_X(M,GN)$ with the pro-etale mapping systems $\mathcal H_Y(
u_Y^*FM,
u_Y^*N)$ and $\mathcal H_X(
u_X^*M,
u_X^*GN)$ of [lem-coef-system-internal-hom-representability], it gives an isomorphism between these in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$. Applying $R\lim$ gives inverse isomorphisms in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, with the same naturality and projection identities. Neither the inverse equations nor the transposes are inferred solely from finite evaluations.

Agent-formulated ordinary-system refinement; argument allocation and the complete retained argument are in the worker report.

proof.text:
Put $A=\widehat{\mathcal H}_Y(FM,N)$ and $B=\widehat{\mathcal H}_X(M,GN)$. By [lem-coef-system-internal-hom-representability], for every $P\in D(\mathscr S_s^{\mathrm{et}})$ these represent the indicated tensor-Hom functors. Write $\theta_P:\operatorname{Hom}(P,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(a_Y^*P\otimes^L FM,N)$ and $\lambda_P:\operatorname{Hom}(P,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(a_X^*P\otimes^L M,GN)$ for their natural representing bijections. Let $\pi_{P,M}$ be the canonical invertible projection in the hypothesis; [lem-coef-system-compact-support-projection] identifies it as an actual natural system map with the canonical finite evaluations. Define
$$J_P=\lambda_P^{-1}\circ\Psi\circ(-\circ\pi_{P,M}^{-1})\circ\theta_P,$$
where $\Psi$ is the actual $F\dashv G$ Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], applied to $a_X^*P\otimes^LM$ and $N$. All four arrows are bijections. Their naturality in $P$, in $M$ contravariantly and in $N$ covariantly follows from naturality of their stated factors.

source.place: Second paragraph, middle RHom isomorphism: all coefficient-system tests, before inverse limit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in $D(\mathscr S_s^{\mathrm{et}})$ to the natural transformations $J$ and $J^{-1}$. They give unique maps $\widehat\Phi:A\to B$ and $\widehat\Psi:B\to A$ satisfying $J_P(x)=\widehat\Phi x$ and $J_P^{-1}(y)=\widehat\Psi y$. Thus postcomposition by $\widehat\Psi\widehat\Phi$ and by $1_A$ has the same effect for every $P$, and likewise on $B$. Injectivity in that cited bijection gives $\widehat\Psi\widehat\Phi=1_A$ and $\widehat\Phi\widehat\Psi=1_B$. For maps $M'\to M$, $N\to N'$, naturality of $J_P$ from step 1 gives the two naturality squares after postcomposition with every $P\to A$; the same injectivity proves the squares in the coefficient-system category.

source.place: Second and final paragraphs: representing isomorphism and inverse equations in the system category.

proof.text:
Let $v_X:a_X^*B\otimes^LM\to GN$ correspond to $1_B$ under $\lambda_B$. Reading $J_B^{-1}(1_B)$ from right to left shows that $\widehat\Psi$ is represented by
$$a_Y^*B\otimes^LFM\xrightarrow{\pi_{B,M}}F(a_X^*B\otimes^LM)\xrightarrow{F(v_X)}FGN\xrightarrow{\epsilon_N}N.$$
Here [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives exactly $\Psi^{-1}(g)=\epsilon_NF(g)$, so this uses the specified counit. Conversely, if $v_Y:a_Y^*A\otimes^LFM\to N$ represents $1_A$, then $\widehat\Phi$ is represented by $G(v_Y\pi_{A,M}^{-1})\eta_{a_X^*A\otimes^LM}$. These are the two transposes of the bijections used in step 1, rather than independently chosen maps with those evaluations.

source.place: Second paragraph, middle RHom isomorphism: explicit inverse transpose through the actual counit.

proof.text: Under the conditional counit-compatible identification with $F_n\dashv G_n$, evaluate the explicit inverse composite of step 3. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], tensor, derived pushforward, closed evaluation and their specified transposes evaluate to the finite constructions; the internal-Hom evaluation applies because the first inputs $M$ and $FM$ are normalized. The representing objects have these evaluation identifications by [lem-coef-system-internal-hom-representability]. The projection evaluates to $\pi_{n}$ by [lem-coef-system-compact-support-projection]. Consequently $e_n\widehat\Psi$ is the finite transpose of $\epsilon_{n,N_n}F_n(v_{X,n})\pi_{n}$. This is precisely the inverse finite derived mapping-complex adjunction. Since evaluation preserves the inverse equations already proved in step 2, $e_n\widehat\Phi$ is its inverse, the forward finite adjunction. No equality in step 2 was inferred from evaluation.

source.place: Second paragraph, finite RHom isomorphism: evaluation of the constructed inverse.

proof.text: Take $P=\mathbf1$ in step 1. The canonical $\pi_{\mathbf1,M}$ is the identity after tensor-unit identifications: for its proper part this is the unit formula of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied to the ringed sequence sites; its open tensor part sends $m\otimes1$ to $m\otimes1$, hence is the identity under the unit identifications. The ordinary adjunction formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] therefore give $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_NF(g)$ on degree-zero Hom. The projection identities for arbitrary $P$ are exactly the defining equations $\lambda_P(\widehat\Phi x)=\Psi(\theta_P(x)\pi_{P,M}^{-1})$ and $\theta_P(\widehat\Psi y)=\epsilon_NF(\lambda_P(y))\pi_{P,M}$ from steps 1 and 3; both hold as actual system equations.

source.place: Second and final paragraphs: degree-zero adjunction and the projection equations.

proof.text:
For $(FM,N)$ on $Y$ and $(M,GN)$ on $X$, all four inputs are normalized with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels by hypothesis. Thus [lem-coef-system-internal-hom-representability] supplies natural, evaluation- and transpose-preserving isomorphisms $c_Y:UA\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_Y(
u_Y^*FM,
u_Y^*N)$ and $c_X:UB\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_X(
u_X^*M,
u_X^*GN)$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$, where $U$ takes the underlying abelian tower. Put $\Phi^{\mathrm{Tow}}=c_XU(\widehat\Phi)c_Y^{-1}$ and $\Psi^{\mathrm{Tow}}=c_YU(\widehat\Psi)c_X^{-1}$. Their products are identities by cancellation and step 2. Naturality and the two projection equations of step 5 are carried to the corresponding equations under these stated natural comparisons.

source.place: Second paragraph, both ends of the finite RHom comparison: etale representing objects to pro-etale mapping towers.

proof.text: Apply the actual functor $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], specialized to modules over $\mathbf Z$ on the one-point site. Functoriality sends the two products in step 6 to $R\lim(1)=1$, so $R\lim\Phi^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ and $R\lim\Psi^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ are inverse. Applying that same functor to each naturality or projection equation preserves it. This uses total derived limit on the ordinary derived tower category, not a choice of morphisms between homotopy-limit triangles.

source.place: Final paragraph: triangle/inverse identities before the derived limit, then functorial passage to it.

proof_origin.place: Second paragraph middle RHom isomorphism and final paragraph; explicit representing-system refinement using Stacks 001P, 07A6, 08J9, 0B56 and 0941.
